note: mapping_basis=data_labels: the .do keeps REG12A's own columns P1202A-P1202F and sets item = the source column name (core model s3 pattern 1, no rename). The data dictionary's variable labels tie P1202A..F to the questionnaire's rows A..F, 6/6 in order, same letters, so there is no numbering offset here (unlike the public and permission siblings). RESP: NOT recoded. Bookmark 1 only sets 9 (NR) to missing; its header comment reads 'scale: 1 Muy de acuerdo, 2 De acuerdo, 3 Desacuerdo', matching the dictionary value labels and the printed column order (Muy de acuerdo 1, De acuerdo 2, Desacuerdo 3). option_text keyed to those codes. Route 9 (raw REG12A vs irw_fetch live): identity reading matches 18/18 item x resp cells; a reversed (1<->3) reading matches only the 6 middle (resp 2) cells. Live 1/2/3 = raw 1/2/3: P1202A 368/995/1910, P1202B 1493/1663/117, P1202C 227/653/2394, P1202D 175/730/2369, P1202E 412/1461/1392, P1202F 25/166/3081. Per-respondent check with id rebuilt as the .do does (sort UPM NVIVI NHOGA, id=_n): 19631/19631 id x item cells equal, 0 raw-only, 0 live-only. Dropped NR (9): 3/3/2/2/11/4 = 25; live 19631 rows = 3276 x 6 - 25 (the .do asserts 19631), 3275 ids. Direction is also content-coherent: 'mismo derecho ... a trabajar' (B) is 96% agree, 'obligación ... relaciones sexuales ... aunque ella no quiera' (F) 94% Desacuerdo. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (6 items, resp {1,2,3}); every item has an option row for all 3 levels, all 3 used by every item (per-item n 3265-3274, E lowest from its 11 NR). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = each printed 1202 row verbatim with the row letter dropped ('A. ', 'B.' etc.; B and E print no space after the letter) and the line-break hyphen in C ('prin-cipal', which the PDF text layer and the dictionary both read 'principal') joined. The trailing '…' that the questionnaire prints on rows C, D, E and F (not on A or B) is kept as printed; the dictionary labels omit it. The 1202 stem 'Ante las siguientes afirmaciones, dígame si usted está muy de acuerdo, de acuerdo o en desacuerdo.' is a complete read-aloud sentence applying to all six rows, so it goes in instructions (the dictionary has the same text without the final period), not joined into item_text as the fragment stems of 1203/1120 were. The 'ENCUESTADORA: LEA CADA ALTERNATIVA PAUSADAMENTE Y MARQUE EL CÓDIGO ...' block and the manual's 'Esta pregunta permite investigar la percepción...' are interviewer-facing and not shipped. option_text = the printed column headers with line-break hyphens joined ('De acuer-do', 'Des-acuer-do' -> 'De acuerdo', 'Desacuerdo'), identical to the dictionary value labels; no row for NR 9. Single section_id, no section_prompt. language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation: INE publishes the ENSIMUP in Spanish only; all English produced by IRW. STEP 3b: dictionary Description ('Agreement with statements about traditional gender roles in the household, including expenses, work, housework, obedience, and sexual obligation') matches 1202 rows A-F (expenses, work, housework, obedience, friends, sexual obligation); 6 live items = 6 printed rows; 3-level resp = the 3-point agreement scale. RIGHTS: originator INE Paraguay; neither the questionnaire nor the manual cites an upstream instrument for 1202 (the manual's only external citations are the OMS definition of sexual violence and INEGI's ENDIREH 2016 marco conceptual, and INEGI carries a ship verdict in instrument_rights_register.csv in any case).
